record.original_question: Can one find a combinatorial analogue of the quotient criterion for coverings that works beyond the regular and chiral cases?

evidence.quote: Problem 3. Find a combinatorial analogue of the quotient criterion.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope of rank n is a partially ordered set P (whose elements are called faces) with a unique minimum face and unique maximum face, in which every maximal chain (flag) has the same length n+1, which is strongly flag-connected, and which satisfies the diamond condition: whenever F < G are faces with rank(G) = rank(F) + 2, there are exactly two faces H with F < H < G. The set of flags F(P) carries, for each i ∈ {0,1,…,n−1}, an involution which sends a flag Φ to the unique flag Φ^i differing from Φ only in its rank-i face; these are the flag-adjacency relations.

A surjective rank- and adjacency-preserving map η : P → Q between abstract polytopes of the same rank is called a covering. The polytope P is regular if its automorphism group acts transitively on F(P), and chiral if this group has exactly two orbits on F(P) such that adjacent flags lie in different orbits. More generally, P is a k-orbit polytope if Aut(P) has exactly k orbits on F(P).

For regular polytopes there is a classical quotient criterion: a regular polytope R covers a regular polytope Q if and only if Q ≅ R/N for some subgroup N of Aut(R) satisfying an explicit intersection condition on the distinguished generators. An analogous quotient criterion has been established for chiral polytopes.

Problem. Formulate and prove a purely combinatorial quotient criterion for coverings of abstract polytopes that applies to k-orbit polytopes for arbitrary k, and in particular yields a necessary and sufficient combinatorial condition (without restriction to the regular or chiral cases) under which one abstract polytope covers another.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears as Problem 3 in a 2016 list of open problems on k-orbit polytopes. No published resolution providing a combinatorial analogue of the quotient criterion for general k-orbit polytopes was found; subsequent work treats specific symmetry classes but does not establish a general criterion.
